title: TypeScript and input you cannot trust

questions.why: An empty text converts to 0. That is why the blank check must come before converting.

wrong.0: That is `Number("abc")`. Empty text is a special case: 0.
wrong.3: `Number` does not throw; it converts silently.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-162: parts 15, 15, 15, 15 and the exam blank. What is the total?
questions.why: A total exists only when every part is a number. A blank exam means "not entered".

wrong.0: That counts the blank exam as 0. A blank is not a zero.
wrong.2: The exam has no mark at all.
wrong.3: 60 is the raw CA. It is not a final result.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-162: Individual 12, Class Test 13.5, Group 14, Project 10, Exam 68/100. What is the Final?

wrong.0: That adds the raw marks without scaling.
wrong.2: The rule keeps two decimals; it does not round to a whole number.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-171: a JHS 2 exam marked 112 out of 140. What is the exam scaled to 50?

wrong.1: That is the JHS 3 mock scale, out of 70.
wrong.2: The exam is not scaled at all here.
wrong.3: 80 is the percentage. The final uses the exam scaled to 50.

questions.prompt: A pupil was absent for Group Work, and the teacher types ABS. What does the total show?
options: Nothing: the result is incomplete, and it records that there is an absence
0 for that part, and a total
The average of the other parts
questions.why: ABS is a valid entry, but no total exists unless every part is a number.

wrong.1: That invents a zero for a pupil who was not there.
wrong.2: No rule says to average. That would invent a mark.
wrong.3: ABS is allowed. The teacher must be able to record it.

questions.prompt: Find the mistake: `const mark = input || null`
questions.why: `||` treats 0 as false, so it picks `null`. Use a check with `=== null` or `??`.

wrong.0: `||` works with any values. That is the problem: it works too well.
wrong.2: `const` can hold any value, null included.
wrong.3: A pupil who scored 0 would show as blank.

questions.prompt: Which type is right for a value that comes from a form?
questions.why: `unknown` means "could be anything; check before use". TypeScript enforces the check.

wrong.1: It might be missing, or a number. You do not know yet.
wrong.3: `never` is a type with no values at all.

questions.prompt: What does `parseFloat("12abc")` give, and what must a strict mark parser do with `"12abc"`?
questions.why: parseFloat reads digits until it meets something else. A strict parser matches the whole text and refuses.

wrong.0: parseFloat stops at the first letter and returns what it read: 12.
wrong.2: Accepting 12 silently drops what the teacher typed.
wrong.3: parseFloat returns a number, never text.
